tldr: For exact exogenous \(F_m\) and a known positive invertible binary bridge \(B\), the map \(K\mapsto T=KB\) embeds the causal fiber in the classical nonnegative binary stochastic-root class, and four strict affine inequalities are exactly what transfers a root back through \(B^{-1}\) to a positive causal channel.  This yields the exhaustive odd/even fiber table, the rank-one exception, and the endpoint-fixed orbit classification.  Affine and polynomial queries are then certified by evaluating the finite fiber: singleton cells admit every query, while an even two-root cell uses the ring generated by \(r^2\) and an odd-coefficient normal-form test with naive \(O(Nd^2)\) coefficient complexity.  A rational asymmetric family has effects \(\pm a\) with rational \(a\in(0,1)\) arbitrarily close to one, proving the sharp worst-case diameter supremum \(2\); the original \(\pm1/5\) pair remains a worked instance.  The contribution is an incremental framework-specific bridge filter, endpoint-fixed orbit audit, and exact query certificate built on classical binary-root enumeration.
